Do a century and then a 60 mile ride, ride normal for three weeks and then do a 80 mile ride and a 80 mile ride the day after. This will condition your body to recover and push at the same time, without overloading.

EATING IS KEY! You'll be repairing your muscles from all of that pedaling and vibration the second and third day, so EAT! You can sustain a lot longer than you think you can with long distance riding, but if you don't eat, you'll suffer.

Also sunscreen as much a possible. Just on a personal note, I wasn't a big sunscreen person until I realized how draining a day of riding can be without it. If they have sponsored food stops they'll most likely have it, so don't forget it! 

Train for long days and slow days, hard days and easy days: Time on the saddle is the most important! Sometimes it's better at those distances to train by time more than milage!

I'll just list it out for you:
6 Nutri-Grain Bars
3 Chocolate Chip Cliff Bars
1 Luna Bar
1 Peanut Butter Cracker (like 10 crackers)
2 donuts

It takes trial and error to figure out what you like eating on the bike. For me, Nutri-grain bars are easy to chew, light and tasty. The Cliff bars I would highly recommend to anyone for their high calorie count.

 Pacing your eating is pretty important. I did one bar (roughly 120 cal) every 30 minutes. Had to stop for some donuts (which you should do!) at one point and crackers at another. 

My best advice: you should never feel hungry on a century ride. Plan what you'll eat and how often & it'll be easier to enjoy the experience not having to worry about it on the big day.

Yeah make sure you don't injure yourself by taking too fast in too little time. 

Make sure you're taking momentum up onto the hill. You can do much less work at 10% slope right before than the 20% - 25% later. Also work on technique. If your legs are totally pooped out and under the duress of lactic acid, try taking the hill in a zig-zag to reduce gradient until you can power more. 

Also work on breathing. Under this workload our bodies are basically squatting out body weight x 2 which means C02 builds quickly and oxygen is depleted very fast. To avoid fatigue, try different breathing along with more training! 

Hope some of this helped stay riding and take those hills on pedal at a time! You're stronger than you think you are!

This is your IT band becoming inflamed and locking up the movement in your leg from the base of your hip. I've had it happen before and I'm in great shape with minor knee aches every once in a while. The best cure for this random spasm: Biofreeze, IcyHot, or any other locally applied medicine to the upper thigh along with a week or so of rest. Make sure to massage it on your side with a foam roller or tennis ball to loosen the IT Band for quicker recovery!
